To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) lipread information affects sound perception; (ii) the effect of lipread information depends on whether the two information sources were assigned to the same object; and (iii) the effect of the lipread information depends also on the current state of the system, which can be either speech or non-speech mode.
(a) the brain uses multisensory information to infer causality, and (b) this inference process is adaptive.

the causal inference problem is solved in speech processing in a similar fashion as it is in other domains, namely by using the information available in the auditory signal itself to infer the causal structure.
